director.question: q2
director.why: q2 offers the most information at 0.256 bits and directly tests persistence of the Type II plateau above 60 uJy versus fading alternatives

question.text: Brighter in r three days from now than at its last r detection?

risky.text: Brighter than 60 microjansky in r 5 days from now?

payload.rule: Every ZTF g or r measurement taken after this bet was sealed, up to one day past its last forecast, is scored against the forecast, interpolated linearly between days. The question is settled by the first r measurement within a day of its time; a limit above the reference leaves it void.

instrument.why: Stable ~19 mag detections across four nights after deep limits with consistent intra-night repeats and high real stamp score indicate a sky source, not detector noise.

implausible.why: x1 of -3.0 implies an extreme fast-declining subluminous Ia that must be intrinsically red, but fitted c ~0.0 is normal-blue and inconsistent with the observed flat post-peak lightcurve.

Fitted peak at -29.1 d is ~8 d before deep non-detections at -21.5 d while later detections are brighter than those limits, requiring a rise after peak that is inconsistent with monotonic Ibc decline.

theories.argument: The r-band shows a flat ~19 mag (~90 uJy) plateau over 4 days after deep pre-explosion limits to ~19.8 mag, fit excellently by a Type II at z=0.087 with chi2/point=0.09 and peak at -17.9 d in the observing gap. The high-latitude (55 deg) real stamp with p=0.92 offset from a bright galaxy supports a hydrogen-rich extragalactic explosion on plateau.

refuted_if.why: A Type IIP ~20 days past peak should still be on its ~90 uJy plateau and cannot fade by half in a few days.

theories.weakest_point: The case rests on only five single-band r detections with no color, no observed rise, and no plateau drop to anchor the redshift and explosion epoch.

theories.argument: The five r-band detections near 19 mag just after the fitted maximum at -7.1 d are well fit by a z=0.105 SN Ia with chi2 per point of 0.22. Deep pre-explosion limits to 19.4-19.8 mag before day -21 and a clean real stamp offset from a galaxy at high latitude are consistent with an extragalactic Ia rise.

refuted_if.why: By 12 days past maximum a x1=-3 Ia at z=0.105 must have faded well below peak to r fainter than ~19.5 mag (~60 uJy).

theories.weakest_point: The fit requires extreme fast-decliner x1=-3.0 at the prior edge yet the observed r-band is flat over four days instead of declining rapidly, with no g-band color to confirm Ia evolution.

theories.argument: The five r-band detections near 19 mag over four days with p_real 0.92 offset from a bright galaxy match a stripped-envelope supernova at z 0.0578 seen about three weeks after its fitted peak on a slowly declining tail, and the fit achieves chi2 per point 0.12 with no limit violations. The flat short-term evolution is plausible for an Ib/c slowing toward its cobalt-powered tail with no rebrighteni

refuted_if.why: A stripped-envelope tail about four weeks after peak must fade steadily, so unchanged brightness after a week would contradict cobalt-powered decline.

theories.weakest_point: The case rests only on single-band flat photometry with no color, rise, or decline shape, and the fit places peak about 23 days before first detection while carrying the lowest supernova weight at 0.1

wording.text: It is likely that the object will still appear brighter than the set limit in red light five days from now.
